doom.driver: Iran sets conditions for opening Strait of Hormuz after UAE says one of its ships was targeted by airstrike.
doom.blurb: DEAL STILL A MIRAGE, MISSILES STILL FLYING
doom.summary: That 'breakthrough' Bessent was teasing earlier this week? Iran just responded by adding more conditions and letting the Houthis take a shot at an Aramco facility for good measure. The Strait remains closed, tanker crews remain in limbo, and the diplomacy is moving at the speed of a fully-laden VLCC sailing through a minefield. Meanwhile Saudi Arabia says the Aramco fire is out, which is the geopolitical equivalent of 'everything's fine' while the building is still smoldering.

factors.name: Geopolitics
factors.detail: Hormuz talks dragging with Iran adding new conditions, a UAE ship targeted, and Houthis striking Aramco — de-escalation is not happening on schedule.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: Todd Blanche confirmed as US Attorney General despite Republican dissent, raising questions about the independence of federal law enforcement.

factors.name: AI Capability
factors.detail: OpenAI accidentally attacked Hugging Face in a cyber incident — AI systems are increasingly capable of causing collateral damage even unintentionally.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: Hardware backdoors discovered in some x86 CPUs — a quiet but deeply unsettling finding that could have supply-chain security implications at scale.

factors.name: Alignment
factors.detail: AI barons pledging philanthropic fortunes is either encouraging or a distraction from the systems they're building — probably both.

doom.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing — weather-dominated scene, a thick petrochemical haze and salt fog rolls across the Strait of Hormuz at midday, the brutal Gulf summer sun reduced to a smoldering orange smear behind curtains of grey-brown atmospheric murk, deep navy water below churning with heat shimmer and mist, the narrow chokepoint geography visible as two dark coastlines — rocky brown Iranian cliffs to the north, flat sandy UAE shore to the south — pressing in from both edges of the frame, the strait itself clogged with dozens of anchored supertankers rendered as dense silhouettes of dark red and black hull shapes barely visible through the haze, a massive VLCC in the foreground showing a blackened jagged wound low on its maroon hull with dark smoke wisping upward and dissolving into the fog, the Iranian coastline to the north hinting at angular concrete emplacements half-swallowed by atmospheric murk, the entire scene color-graded in deep navy and smoldering orange, smoke-filtered light casting no clean shadows, warmth feeling threatening, the fog itself the dominant presence swallowing the world's most critical shipping lane into an ominous amber-grey void.

dawn.blurb: THE SUN ITSELF NOW POWERS QUANTUM TECHNOLOGY
dawn.summary: In a week where the news has been heavy with missile shortages, new defence pacts, and geopolitical standoffs, scientists quietly pulled off something remarkable: generating quantum entanglement using ordinary sunlight rather than energy-hungry lasers. This isn't incremental progress — it's a fundamental rethink of how quantum technology can be powered, potentially making it vastly more accessible and sustainable. When the sun can do the work of a precision laser, the future of quantum computing just got a little warmer and a lot more democratic.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: Generating quantum entanglement from sunlight outdoors overturns a core assumption of quantum technology and opens the door to low-energy, scalable quantum systems.

factors.name: Environment
factors.detail: Replacing power-intensive lasers with sunlight for quantum processes could significantly reduce the energy footprint of next-generation computing infrastructure.

factors.name: Cooperation
factors.detail: Iran's President Pezeshkian publicly called for an end to deadlock with the US, signalling that at least one side sees this moment as ripe for a lasting agreement.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: The Perseverance rover's autonomous driving record — 90% of its Martian distance covered without human input — reflects decades of engineering ambition finally paying off on another world.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: A new wearable ultrasound patch was shown to boost REM sleep by 43 minutes without drugs or surgery, offering a drug-free path to better mental and physical recovery for millions.

dawn.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. Extreme close-up filling the entire frame, a single small glass prism resting on a sun-warmed surface, its interior blazing with captured golden amber light, deep warm teal shadows pooling at its base edges. From within the prism's core, two identical golden-white motes of light drift apart in opposite directions simultaneously, connected by a hair-thin luminous thread, the entangled pair made visible as a symbolic metaphor for something that cannot be separated. The prism's facets throw fractured rainbow slivers across the frame edges, hinting at an open-sky outdoor world beyond. The glass itself glows from within, overwhelmed by sunlight rather than any artificial source, warm amber saturating every surface. Long raking side-light cuts across the prism's geometry, casting a crisp cold teal shadow to the left while the right face burns molten gold. The twin light-motes float symmetrically outward from the same point of origin, mirror images, indistinguishable, impossibly linked — the entire image a meditation on hidden connection born from abundance.
